annotations.title: What the vaults you hold share

description: READ THE VAULTS YOU HOLD TOGETHER. This one is about a SET rather than a single subject; an allocator does not hold one subject. This answers the three questions that only exist across holdings and that no vault page can show you: a CONTROLLER behind more than one of them, a MARKET behind more than one of them, and an EXIT that is not the sum of the exits. It is a screen, not advice: there is no allocation percentage and no expected return in this answer and there never will be. THE EXIT IS FOUR FIGURES AND THEY ARE NEVER ADDED UP — `declared` (the venue publishes a withdrawable figure), `behind-a-queue` (we have READ that a request comes first, so nothing leaves today at any price whatever cash is sitting there), `floor-only` (the only reading is uninvested cash, a lower bound) and `unread` — because a portfolio that is 40% readable is not a portfolio that is 40% liquid. A queue OUTRANKS a declared figure: a vault can publish a number and still take a request first, and the number is then what a request settles from. The exit split, the coverage and the bands are FREE, and so is every per-vault reading behind them at `vault_check`; a plan buys what the holdings SHARE. It cannot verify that you hold any of this.

holdings.description: The vaults you hold, as `slug:usd,slug:usd`. The amount after each slug is OPTIONAL and the answer is useful without it: leave it off and every figure counts holdings rather than dollars, and `positionsNotStated` says how many. Where you price SOME of them, a shared exposure whose sharers are not all priced reports `positionUsd: null` rather than a partial sum, because a partial sum reads as a complete one. At most 50 holdings.

name: portfolio_screen

byRiskBand.description: Holdings per published risk band, with `unread` as its own key rather than folded into low.

cannotSee.description: What this answer does not contain, starting with the fact that we cannot verify you hold any of it, and ending with the fact that it is not advice.

coverage.description: The share of your holdings carrying each reading at all: `risk`, `exit`, `control`, `markets`. A control band of `unknown` counts as UNREAD, because it is.

exit.description: FOUR CLASSES, NEVER SUMMED: `declared`, `behind-a-queue`, `floor-only`, `unread`, each with `holdings` and `positionUsd`. Read `behind-a-queue` first: that is money nothing can be taken from today.

meta.description: How current this answer is and what it was read from: `freshness` and the ages behind it. Present on every answer from this server, whatever the tool.

notHeld.description: The slugs we do not hold at all, LISTED rather than dropped: a portfolio quietly one short is the wrong answer to the question you asked.

positionUsd.description: The total you stated, over the holdings you priced. Null where you priced none.

positionsNotStated.description: Holdings you named without an amount. Every dollar figure in this answer excludes them.

resolved.description: How many of them we hold a vault for.

says.description: The findings in words, including what was not stated.

sharedControllers.description: PAID. Controllers that can move the money in MORE THAN ONE of your holdings, with the slugs and your stated position behind each. Reading the vaults one at a time shows one controller each; held together they are one bet. NULL where withheld, which `detailRequires` states — never read a null here as "nothing is shared".

sharedMarkets.description: PAID. Markets or collateral more than one holding lends against. A vault page gives your share OF that market; this says how much of YOUR money is behind it. NULL where withheld.

sharedVenues.description: PAID. Venues and chains carrying more than one holding. NULL where withheld.

warnings.description: Anything the server wants a caller to know about THIS answer before acting on it. Empty is the normal case and is not a guarantee.

title: What the vaults you hold share
